questions.question: Which clinical triad characterises normal pressure hydrocephalus?

answers.text: Gait apraxia, cognitive decline, urinary incontinence

questions.explanation: Hakim's triad: gait disturbance (usually first and most responsive to shunting), dementia, urinary incontinence. Ophthalmoplegia/ataxia/confusion is Wernicke's encephalopathy.

questions.question: Which features should prompt emergency MRI for suspected cauda equina syndrome? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Red flags: saddle/perineal sensory loss, bladder dysfunction (retention with overflow), bowel dysfunction, reduced anal tone, bilateral sciatica. Isolated unilateral radicular pain is not a red flag.

flashcards.front: First-line drug for classical trigeminal neuralgia?

flashcards.back: Cerebellar tonsillar descent **≥ 5 mm** below the foramen magnum (McRae line).

flashcards.definition: Hemicord lesion: ipsilateral weakness and loss of proprioception/vibration, contralateral loss of pain and temperature below the lesion.

cases.title: Sudden headache in a 48-year-old
cases.presentation: A 48-year-old smoker presents with sudden 'worst ever' headache during exertion, followed by vomiting. GCS 14 (E3V5M6), neck stiffness, no focal deficit. BP 170/95.

stages.title: Initial workup
stages.content: You are called from the emergency department.
stages.question: What is your immediate investigation and what would you do if it is negative at 12 hours?
stages.answer: Non-contrast CT head (sensitivity near 100% within 6 h). If negative beyond 6 h, lumbar puncture ≥ 12 h from ictus for xanthochromia (spectrophotometry).

stages.title: Imaging
stages.content: CT shows diffuse basal cistern SAH with thick clot. CTA shows a 7 mm AComm aneurysm.
stages.question: Grade this patient and outline the key early management.
stages.answer: WFNS grade 2 (GCS 14, no deficit); modified Fisher 3-4 depending on IVH. Secure the aneurysm early (within 24-72 h) by coiling or clipping per MDT; nimodipine 60 mg 4-hourly for 21 days; euvolaemia; BP control until secured; monitor for hydrocephalus.

stages.title: Day 6
stages.content: She becomes confused with new right leg weakness. Sodium 131.
stages.question: Differential and management?
stages.answer: Delayed cerebral ischaemia from vasospasm (ACA territory), hydrocephalus, hyponatraemia (cerebral salt wasting vs SIADH), seizure, rebleed. CT/CTA/CTP, maintain euvolaemia, induced hypertension, correct sodium without fluid restriction, consider endovascular therapy (angioplasty/intra-arterial vasodilators).

cases.discussion: Key points: timing of LP, grading scales (WFNS, Hunt & Hess, modified Fisher), ISAT favouring coiling where both options are feasible, nimodipine as the only drug shown to improve outcome, and fluid restriction avoided in SAH-related hyponatraemia.
